title: The Cabin Phone
hook: The cabin's old phone had no cord. The guestbook said: if it rings, don't answer, and never say your name inside.
lines: The cabin I rented had an old rotary phone on the kitchen wall.
Its cord had been cut. It just hung there... like a dead tail.
The guestbook had one rule, underlined twice.
If the phone rings, don't answer it. And never say your name inside this cabin.
The first night was perfect. Snow. Firewood. Total silence.
Then, at three in the morning... it rang.
That old metal bell shook the whole wall. Twelve times. Then it stopped.
And from the dark kitchen, very quietly... someone picked it up.
A man's voice said, Yes. She's here. She's asleep.
Footsteps crossed the floor. My bedroom door creaked open.
He leaned over my bed and whispered... What's your name?
I didn't answer. I didn't breathe. At dawn, he was gone.
I packed fast. On my way out, I signed the guestbook... out of habit. My full name.
That night, at home, my phone started ringing. The caller I.D. just said... Cabin.
